blocks.content: GraphQL is not just a different way to format API requests. It's a completely different model for thinking about data.
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1785396018498-401198708.png
blocks.alt: GraphQL replaces fixed endpoint shapes with a client-described query, avoiding over and under-fetching entirely

blocks.content: Instead of a server exposing fixed endpoints that return fixed shapes, GraphQL exposes a single endpoint where the client describes exactly what data it needs  and that's exactly what it gets back.

1. GraphQL SDL (Schema Definition Language)

["Defines your entire API structure what data exists and how types are related","Each type is like a model (User, Post, Comment) with fields and relationships","! → non-null (always present), [Post!]! → list + items both non-null","Types can reference each other → forms a graph (User → Post → Comment → User)","Root operations: Query reads data, mutation writes or updates data, and subscription provides real-time updates."]
items: Defines your entire API structure what data exists and how types are related
Each type is like a model (User, Post, Comment) with fields and relationships
! → non-null (always present), [Post!]! → list + items both non-null
Types can reference each other → forms a graph (User → Post → Comment → User)
Root operations: Query reads data, mutation writes or updates data, and subscription provides real-time updates.

blocks.content: GraphQL allows clients to request exactly the data they need (no over- or under-fetching), uses a strongly typed schema for safer and predictable APIs, and provides a single flexible endpoint instead of multiple REST endpoints.
2. Queries ( Reading data )
A Query is how you fetch data. The client writes a query that mirrors the shape of the data it wants. The response JSON has exactly the same shape as the query.

blocks.content: 4. Subscriptions  ( Real-time )
Subscriptions let the client listen for real-time events. Under the hood they use WebSocket. The client opens a persistent connection and the server pushes data whenever the subscribed event fires.

5. Resolvers ( how the server fetches data )
blocks.text: 5. Resolvers ( how the server fetches data )

blocks.content: A resolver is a function on the server that knows how to fetch data for a specific field. When GraphQL receives a query, it walks through every requested field and calls its resolver.

","User field resolvers → fetch posts and followers for each user
","Subscription → listen for real-time comments on a post using pubsub
","_represents unused parent,argscontain inputs,contextholds shared resources like DB and pubsub

blocks.content: 6. The N+1 problem ( the biggest GraphQL pitfall )
blocks.text: 6. The N+1 problem ( the biggest GraphQL pitfall )

blocks.content: This is the most important thing to understand about GraphQL performance. It happens when resolvers are naive about how they fetch data.

A query asks for 10 posts and their authors. The posts resolver fires once and fetches 10 posts. Then for each post, the author resolver fires 10 separate database calls. Total: 1 + 10 = 11 queries. With 100 posts, it's 101 queries.
NAIVE RESOLVER: CAUSES N+1
DATA LOADER: BATCHES INTO 1 CALL
DataLoader collects all the IDs from every resolver in the same tick, then fires a single batched query
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (1,2,3...). 11 queries become 2.
7. Fragments ( Reuse query shapes )
When the same fields appear in multiple queries, fragments let you define them once and reuse everywhere like variables for query shapes.

["FragmentUserBasicdefines reusable fields (id, name, email) for a User
","It is reused in multiple places using...UserBasicto avoid repetition
","QueryGetPostfetches a post, its author, and comment authors using the same fragment
","Inline fragments (... on Type) are used for handling different types in unions/interfaces
","GetSearchResultsreturns different fields depending on whether the result is Post, User, or Comment
","Helps keep queries clean, reusable, and flexible
"]

Inline fragments (... on Type) are used for handling different types in unions/interfaces

blocks.content: 8. Directives ( Conditional fields )
Directives let you conditionally include or skip fields based on variables without writing separate queries.
QUERY WITH DIRECTIVES
VARIABLES
9. Error handling
GraphQL always returns 200 OK even on errors. Instead of HTTP error codes, errors are in a top-level errors array alongside the data. Partial data + errors can coexist.
PARTIAL ERROR RESPONSE
CUSTOM ERROR CODES IN RESOLVER
10. Introspection (Self-documenting)
One of GraphQL's superpowers: you can query the schema itself. Tools like GraphiQL and Apollo Studio use this to auto-generate documentation and enable autocomplete.

["Introspection lets clients explore the GraphQL schema dynamically
","__schema→ returns all available types in the API with their kind
","__type(name: \"User\")→ returns all fields of the User type
","Helps discover fields like id, name, email, posts, followers
","Powers tools like GraphiQL to auto-generate API documentation
","Useful for debugging, learning, and building dynamic clients
"]
items: Introspection lets clients explore the GraphQL schema dynamically
__schema→ returns all available types in the API with their kind
__type(name: "User")→ returns all fields of the User type
Helps discover fields like id, name, email, posts, followers
Powers tools like GraphiQL to auto-generate API documentation
Useful for debugging, learning, and building dynamic clients
